What is the difference between a shallow "empty" check written as len(x) == 0 and if not x ?

Supplied answer
Both work, but if not x: is the Pythonic form and it also covers None. len(x) == 0 crashes with TypeError if
x happens to be None, so prefer if not x: unless you specifically need to distinguish an empty container
from None.
